subject: Measurement granularity & short-burst p95 carveout for hosted API
messages:
From: Elena Voss <elena.voss@neptuneanalytics.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency measurement question for hosted inference (p50/p95)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this call with us earlier. To summarize Neptune's ask: we run a streaming inference workload that is highly bursty — short spikes of concurrent requests coming from our edge gateways (typically 30–120s) that push a small percentage of our traffic above your published p95 targets. Our concern is that the p95 calc over long windows (1h) unfairly penalizes these transient bursts and risks an SLA violation despite steady long-run behavior.

Attached is a 2-hour sample traffic dump (traffic-snapshot-20260928.jsonl) showing three spikes during business hours. Can Redwood offer either:
- a short-burst carveout (e.g., ignore contiguous fault windows under X seconds or under Y% of traffic), or
- an alternate measurement granularity (sliding 5m windows aggregated into a weighted-hour) that better reflects user-facing latency?

Commercially, we are prepared to accept a temporary windowed exception during our onboarding ramp if we agree on clear detection and rollback criteria (mutual action plan + telemetry we both can observe). We will need this formalized before signing the Dedicated commitment addendum.

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood proposes measurement approach + guardrails by end of week
- Neptune shares 7 days of traffic telemetry and approves proposed detection rules
- If accepted, include 90-day temporary exception clause in addendum + automated alerting to both teams

cc: Sam Jensen (platform), legal TBD.

Best,
Elena
VP Product
Neptune Analytics

Attachment: traffic-snapshot-20260928.jsonl (sample lines: timestamp,req_id,latency_ms,status)
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Elena Voss <elena.voss@neptuneanalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency measurement question for hosted inference (p50/p95)

Elena — thanks for the sample and clear ask. We dug into the dump and agree that short-lived gateway bursts are the primary driver for the p95 spikes. We have two pragmatic approaches that are defensible operationally and contractually:

Option A — Short-burst carveout (recommended for onboarding):
- Define a contiguous "burst window" as periods where traffic > baseline by 3x for >= 30s and <= 15 minutes.
- If a burst window constitutes < 1% of total requests in the measurement epoch, exclude those windows from p95 calculations for a temporary period (e.g., 90 days).
- Must be accompanied by joint telemetry (we will surface the detected windows in the Console and provide a shared GCS/Drive snapshot).

Option B — Sliding-window aggregation:
- Measure p50/p95 over 5-minute sliding windows, compute a weighted aggregate over an hourly epoch (weight by requests per window).
- This preserves short-term visibility while reducing single-window dominance on the hourly p95.

Operational requirements (both options):
- Neptune provides 7 days of production request-level telemetry (anonymized) — sample provided looks good but we need the full shape.
- Redwood will implement detection rules in staging and share a preview of which windows would be exempt for the last 14 days.
- Any exemption is temporary (90 days) and tied to a remediation plan: either traffic shaping at edge, caching prefixing, or request-smoothing on Neptune side.

Commercial terms we propose to Marissa/Legal: allow a temporary carveout with no SLA credit exposure provided joint monitoring is in place and a formal rollback trigger exists (e.g., >2 exemption events in 30 days).

Attached: proposed-measurement-def.pdf (short explainer + math). I looped Marissa and Lauren for pricing & legal gating.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick technical session tomorrow to go over thresholds.

—Aditya
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

> On Tue, Sep 29, 2026 at 3:12 PM Elena Voss <elena.voss@neptuneanalytics.com> wrote:
> > Thanks for taking this call with us earlier...
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Voss <elena.voss@neptuneanalytics.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency measurement question for hosted inference (p50/p95)

Elena / team — appreciate the thoughtful framing. From a commercial/ops perspective we are willing to accept a controlled, temporary carveout aligned to Option A with the following guardrails:

1) Scope & duration: 90-day exception from the effective date of the addendum. During this time Redwood will not levy SLA credits for p95 breaches that fall squarely into detected burst windows as defined by the joint rule-set.

2) Detection & transparency: Redwood will publish detected burst windows to a shared folder daily; Neptune will provide the anonymized telemetry feed (sample referenced above). Both parties must have an oncall contact for alerts.

3) Rollback / escalation: If there are more than two separate exception events that meet the carveout definition within any rolling 30-day period, the exception will be suspended pending a remediation plan and an operational review.

4) Remediation: Neptune must commit to at least one of the following within the 90 days: edge-rate-limiting, request-level caching for stable prefixes, or traffic shaping at source.

5) Doc addendum: we will circulate a light addendum that codifies the above (SLA language + telemetry sharing + termination clause). There will be no change to base pricing; this is a limited operational concession to facilitate onboarding.

Next: Aditya — please send the staging preview of the detected windows and the addendum draft. Elena — once you sign the addendum we'll start the 90-day timer on the exception.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales | Redwood Inference

- We'll sign the addendum once the legal redline pass is complete (Sam and I will coordinate).
- We'll commit to implementing edge-rate-limiting as our primary remediation and will share rollout dates during the technical session.

Please schedule the technical deep-dive tomorrow — 30–45 minutes to walk thresholds and confirm the staging preview. We're in US/Pacific.

Best,
Elena
